prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds revealed in
earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only tells you how often this line type was paid at all.
- If you decide the line is indemnified and no cap, sub-limit or percentage reduction applies,
  take the stated amount as t and give a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. These
  amounts are before such policy arithmetic; apply caps and reductions on top.
- A line type that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies
  do not carry; price it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 1 "Bicycle frame replacement": indemnified in 1 of 2 earlier cases, t = 0 in 1; when indemnified t per pc about 229 (80% range 142 to 392); revealed per pc: 142-349 (case 24)

items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage, so §§7.1.7 and 7.1.9 cover a pre-loss equivalent. The €229 gross estimate is reduced to €118 by the shared €500 mobility cap (§4.2.2), using an estimated allocation factor of 0.52.
The brakes sustained theft damage, so like-for-like replacement is covered under §§7.1.7 and 7.1.9. The €140 gross estimate is reduced rateably to €72 under §4.2.2.
The tracker worked during recovery, and no theft damage or loss of the tracker itself is established. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude its elective replacement.
The second bicycle was not affected by the theft, and routine servicing is independently excluded under §§3.1.6 and 7.1.5.
Neither the helmet nor the lights are identified as stolen or damaged property. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude supplementary purchases made in connection with the claim.

Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary carriage for the damaged bicycle or its repair parts, but §7.1.10 excludes any share attributable to the unrelated purchases. If this is repair freight, €26 gross reduces rateably to €13 under §4.2.2.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) require a necessary covered attendance, which the generic vehicle line does not establish. If substantiated, a €77 gross charge would reduce to about €38 after sharing the mobility cap.
Fitting the replacement frame and brakes is covered under §7.1.7(c), provided it is separate from the labour already billed. The €113 gross estimate reduces rateably to €58 under §4.2.2.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers sundries consumed in the insured repair, but §7.1.10 requires a link to that repair, which this generic line does not establish. If substantiated, €10 gross reduces to about €5 under the shared cap.

Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary apprentice labour on the theft repair, not time spent servicing the second bike or duplicating billed assembly. One eligible hour at €55 gross reduces rateably to €28.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary skilled repair time if allocated to the stolen bicycle and not already billed as assembly. One eligible hour at €39 gross reduces rateably to €20.
The locksmith's attendance at the recovery site was necessary to release the bike and is separately covered by §5.2.2(a). A €35 gross call-out reduces rateably to €18 under §4.2.2.
Section 5.2.2(b) expressly covers cutting and removing the lock that held the recovered bicycle. The two charges at €54 each total €108 gross, reduced rateably to €56 under §4.2.2.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) allow a second attendance only if recovery actually required it; the claim does not explain why it was needed. If substantiated, €35 gross would reduce to about €17 after sharing the mobility cap.

items.description: Mandatory yard storage and release fee
items.rationale: The yard required payment before releasing the bike, so §5.2.2(c) covers the unavoidable third-party fee. €100 plus 19% VAT is €119 gross; the €1,000 recovery cap does not bind, but the shared €500 mobility cap reduces this line to €61.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim processing. This is distinct from the yard's mandatory release fee.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers every labour grade actually used to release the bike, but §7.1.8(g) bars labour already included in the cutting charge. One separately billable hour at €55 gross reduces rateably to €28.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled labour needed to release the bicycle if not already included in the cutting charge. One eligible hour at €39 gross reduces rateably to €20.
